title: Mini Sprint Atelier: 14d micro-win journal
content:
Purpose and constraints:
- Two-week micro-sprint to prove I can sustain 3 focused habits while shipping one small deliverable. Treat this like an evidence-gathering exercise rather than perfection.
- Constraints: 45–90 minute deep work blocks, max 2 sync meetings/day, sleep >= 7hrs target, 3x weekly cardio.

Northstar outcome (14 days):
- Deliver a minimal "debugging playbook" doc + 1 short demo snippet that reduces average time-to-diagnose for infra incidents by measurable margin in my test runs.
- Personal KPIs to track daily: focus-hours (>=2), context-switches (<=6), shallow-tasks cleared (<=5), quality pass rate on demo (>=85%).

Hypotheses and experiments:
1) If I do morning review + single prioritized MIT (most important task) then daily focus-hours will increase by ~40% vs baseline.
   - Experiment: morning review 09:00 (10m), set MIT, block 09:15–10:45 for deep work.
   - Measurement: diary check + toggl-like timer entries.
2) A tiny "diagnostics checklist" reduces wasted time chasing irrelevant logs by >20% in synthetic tests.
   - Experiment: run 5 seeded incidents in staging and compare time-to-root-cause with/without checklist.
3) Quick async feedback loop (5-min demo + comments in PR) will catch at least 1 usability gap before demo stage.
   - Experiment: tag 1 reviewer (Miguel) on a WIP PR and request a 5-min pass.

Daily template (fill after each day):
- Date: 
- Focus windows (start-end, estimate vs actual):
- MIT accomplished? (Y/N) + notes:
- Small wins: (what shipped or unblocked)
- Friction points / blockers: (short)
- Energy / sleep / steps:
- Quick action for tomorrow:

Metrics dashboard (manual tracking):
- Day 1..14: focus-hours (float), context-switches (int), shallow-tasks done (int), time-to-diagnose (min), checklist-used (Y/N)
- Use simple CSV in a sheet if it looks like data is worth plotting.

Week 1 plan (Days 1–7):
- Day 1: assemble checklist skeleton, scope demo case, baseline run of 3 synthetic incidents.
- Day 2: iterate checklist, start writeup. Morning review + blocked deep work.
- Day 3: demo loop with Miguel (async 5-min), collect comments, baseline instrumentation.
- Day 4: polish playbook, run 2 more synthetic incidents.
- Day 5: integrate small fixes, update playbook, prepare short demo clip.
- Day 6: buffer / catchup / wellbeing check (walk + reflect).
- Day 7: internal retro + snapshot metrics + decision whether to continue same experiments week 2.

Retrospective prompts (to run at EOD of Day 7 and Day 14):
- What did I overcommit on? What saved time?
- Which hypothesis had the clearest signal? Which ones were noisy?
- One surprising failure and one unexpectedly small win.
- Concrete change to my routine for the next sprint.

Risks and mitigations:
- Small tasks ballooning: mitigate by strict 60–90 minute cutoff and a follow-up backlog ticket.
- Meetings creeping in: pre-block deep work and mark status in Slack with ETA.
- Data collection laziness: keep the daily template inline in the playbook and spend 3 min at EOD filling it.

Quick wins backlog (priority order):
- (P0) Finalize minimal checklist + smoke test harness.
- (P1) Draft 1-page playbook + 3 annotated screenshots.
- (P2) Short demo clip + 30s voiceover.
- (P3) PR with docs + tagging Miguel for 5-min review.

Notes to self / voice memo pointers:
- If a day feels "off", mark it and call it data; don't erase it.
- Prefer iterations: ship an imperfect checklist and watch what patterns emerge.
- Keep the demo tiny — people pay attention to <60s clips.

Slack reminders (templates):
- Morning: \"Heads up — deep work blocked 9:15–10:45, ping for urgent only.\"
- PR: \"WIP: small playbook + demo clip; 2-min skim welcome @Miguel.\"

Anchors for success (what I'll celebrate):
- A reproducible drop in average time-to-diagnose in my staging runs by >15% (even if small N).
- Filling the daily template for at least 10/14 days.
- Getting at least one reviewer comment that prevents a bad UX decision.

End-of-sprint deliverables (what to upload to Drive):
- playbook-mini.pdf (1 page)
- demo-clip.mp4 (<=60s)
- incident-timing.csv (raw times for each seeded run)
- notes-retro.md (answers to retrospective prompts)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is 2 deep windows a better default than 1? Try both patterns in week 2 if week 1 shows mixed results.
- If checklist helps, how to surface it inside the on-call runbook later? Add an action item to propose it to SRE doc owners.

Sign-off checklist (before celebrating):
- [ ] Playbook readable by someone unfamiliar (ask Nora to skim).
- [ ] Demo plays start-to-end on my laptop and on a different machine (sanity check).
- [ ] Time samples collected and formatted into CSV.

Micro retrospective note (quick, Day 3):
- Small win: morning review made the 90-min block surprisingly focused.
- Blocker: distracted by Slack thread — need clearer do-not-disturb text.
- Next small change: set Slack auto-response for deep windows and move morning review 15m earlier.

---
Drafting style notes (for myself):
- Keep language simple, remove long paragraphs. Use short checklists.
- Keep evidence: dates + times + tickboxes make it easier to claim progress.

If this looks promising after 14 days, next steps: scale to a 4-week experiment, try embedding the checklist as a small playbook card in the Redwood Console incident runbook template and measure impact across a small team.
